data.narrative:
HLabs is a Seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Paul Hetherington that has raised $5M+. The valuation analysis draws on a broader sector universe of nine private peers (including Walden Robotics, Divergent, and Exotec) and one public comparable (277810.KQ), though a sufficiently dense comparable set at the identical stage and valuation tier proved unavailable for direct median analysis.

Given data constraints, the Stage-Progression method is the primary applicable approach. Using total capital raised of $5M as a base proxy and applying a typical 2.5x multiplier for progression from Seed to the next financing round yields an implied valuation of $12M. This single-method triangulation produces a range of $11M (low-end) to $14M (high-end), with a median of $12M. The stage-progression methodology rests on observable step-up patterns in early-stage venture, though it does not incorporate company-specific traction or operational metrics.

The primary limitation is the absence of sufficient same-stage, same-tier robotics peers to ground a peer-median cross-check. A full valuation would benefit from clarity on HLabs' current revenue, unit economics, and technical differentiation relative to the identified peer set. The $11M–$14M range should be treated as a framework pending additional operational and market data.
